approach:clean-room-reimplementation.name: Clean-room reimplementation
approach:clean-room-reimplementation.summary: New engine with the same rules reading the user's own data files; verified against the original's behaviour.

approach:matching-decompilation.name: Matching decompilation
approach:matching-decompilation.summary: Recover source that rebuilds the original bytes, function by function, with the original compiler.

approach:native-hooking.name: Native hooking
approach:native-hooking.summary: Offline single-player runtime modding by code injected into the process; resolve targets by signature or RTTI, not fixed addresses.

approach:patched-donor-engine.name: Patched donor engine
approach:patched-donor-engine.summary: Existing open engine plus reproducible patches and a data/script translation layer for the new game.

approach:static-recompilation.name: Static recompilation
approach:static-recompilation.summary: Translate the original machine code to C/C++ ahead of time and supply a runtime that reimplements the console or OS.

compiler:msvc.name: MSVC
compiler:msvc.summary: Microsoft's C++ compiler; its RTTI layout is what rtti_scan.py reads and its code generation is what matching decomps reproduce.

engine:blam.name: Blam engine
engine:blam.summary: Halo's data-driven engine: tags compiled into per-scenario cache maps, HaloScript bytecode, BSP structures.

engine:gamebryo.name: Gamebryo
engine:gamebryo.summary: Scene-graph engine (Ni* classes: NiNode, NiAVObject, NiTriShape, controllers, streams) used by Oblivion and Fallout 3/NV; its model files are NIFs and its Bethesda physics blocks are bhk*.

engine:openmw.name: OpenMW
engine:openmw.summary: Open-source reimplementation of the Morrowind engine (Bullet physics, Lua API); the donor engine of OpenOblivion, pinned at two revisions (desktop and Android).

finding:android-arm64-gles-translation-c.name: android-arm64-gles-translation-crash
finding:android-arm64-gles-translation-c.summary: On the stock x86_64 Android emulator an arm64-only app that renders through GL4ES/GLES crashes at scene start with a null call inside the ARM translation layer's GLES proxy; host GPU versus software and newer images make no difference, and a native x86_64 build works.

finding:android-arm64-gles-translation-c.oracle: crash reproduced on both images and both renderers; the x86_64 build starts, renders and passes a six-check gate
finding:android-arm64-gles-translation-c.unverified: Real arm64 phones do not use this layer; other emulator images and ARM-native hosts were not tested.

finding:camera-smoothing-after-physics.name: camera-smoothing-after-physics
finding:camera-smoothing-after-physics.summary: A vertical eye-height filter run before physics (Lua onFrame) regressed ascent variation on the real stairs, while the same idea applied inside the camera update after physics did not: sample the post-physics tracked position.
finding:camera-smoothing-after-physics.build: OpenMW 0.52 pin (Lua onFrame runs before physics and the camera update); OpenOblivion desktop paired probes, 2026-10-01
finding:camera-smoothing-after-physics.oracle: paired same-binary runs, view vertical-velocity variation raw to filtered: Lua real ascent 1206.7 to 3008.3 (worse), real descent 2414.0 to 704.3; native post-physics ascent 1321.4 to 535.7, descent 2266.4 to 546.8
finding:camera-smoothing-after-physics.unverified: No run changed only the timing: the Lua and C++ filters are separate implementations, so phase is the best-fitting explanation, not an isolated cause. The Lua filter run post-physics, or the C++ one pre-physics, was not tried.

finding:compiler-tiebreak-residual.name: compiler-tiebreak-residual
finding:compiler-tiebreak-residual.summary: When the only residual in a matching MSVC 6 function is the operand order of equal-cost x87 operations inside inlined bodies, BW1's maintainers conclude it is a c2 tie-break that depends on earlier inliner IL, not on what the source means, and stop to ask whether to accept a fakematch.
finding:compiler-tiebreak-residual.build: BW1 decomp AGENTS.md at revision be339126394b6fe35699f75b1d300623188b1628 (2026-10-06)
finding:compiler-tiebreak-residual.unverified: Stated by the BW1 maintainers; not reproduced here; MSVC 6 only.

finding:donor-gait-by-animation-state.name: donor-gait-by-animation-state
finding:donor-gait-by-animation-state.summary: OpenMW's borrowed movement picks run or sneak speed only while the actor's animation state is run or sneak; with no TES4 locomotion animations the player always moves at the 150 units/s walk speed, so key-binding changes cannot produce a second gait.
finding:donor-gait-by-animation-state.build: OpenMW 0.52/0.51 pins as used by OpenOblivion preview builds 0.6 to 0.8
finding:donor-gait-by-animation-state.oracle: desktop probe: walk, run and sneak requests all measured 150 while the engine reported a run speed of 337.5; phone logs of 0.7 and 0.8 stayed at median 150 and 149.9
finding:donor-gait-by-animation-state.unverified: Behaviour once TES4 locomotion animations exist.

finding:gl4es-egl-dlopen-startup-deadloc.name: gl4es-egl-dlopen-startup-deadlock
finding:gl4es-egl-dlopen-startup-deadloc.summary: GL4ES's load-time eglGetDisplay can deadlock against the UI RenderThread's driver-init lock while the main thread holds the linker lock in dlopen; calling EGL14.eglGetDisplay on the main thread before the first System.loadLibrary removed the hang (3 of 4 launches hung before, 5 of 5 started after).
finding:gl4es-egl-dlopen-startup-deadloc.build: Android 16 x86_64 emulator, OpenOblivion x86_64 build, 2026-10-06
finding:gl4es-egl-dlopen-startup-deadloc.oracle: debuggerd backtraces of every thread showed the lock cycle; launch outcomes before and after the Java change
finding:gl4es-egl-dlopen-startup-deadloc.unverified: Not observed on real phones; samples of 4 and 5 launches are small.

finding:havok-unit-scale-about-7.name: havok-unit-scale-about-7
finding:havok-unit-scale-about-7.summary: Havok-space values in Oblivion are about 1/7 of game units: hull values read from the running exe divided by its own scale constant (0.14288) give 20.25 and 128 units, and the niftools factor of 7 for packed vertices and the box half-extents measured on door leaves agree.
finding:havok-unit-scale-about-7.build: Oblivion (retail Steam data and exe as in the hull measurement; Vilverin hall gate NIF)
finding:havok-unit-scale-about-7.oracle: two measurements agree: the exe's constant applied to the sampled hull, and box half-extents times 7 reproducing the visible gate slabs
finding:havok-unit-scale-about-7.unverified: The constant is within 0.02% of 1/7 but not exactly it; the niftools factor was cited from that project's tools, not re-read; other Gamebryo games not measured.
finding:havok-unit-scale-about-7.note: confirmed_by cites niftools MaxNifTools.ini (bhkScaleFactor 7) and PyFFI (packed vertices stored as nif/7) as quoted in HAVOK_COLLISION.md

finding:hull-needs-support-point-walkabi.name: hull-needs-support-point-walkability
finding:hull-needs-support-point-walkabi.summary: Giving the player the measured pointed hull alone made the donor solver's stair hack fire (440-480 units/s, distance ratio 1.42 on the stair fixture); judging walkability from the surface under the hull centre instead of the contact normal restored normal climbing.
finding:hull-needs-support-point-walkabi.build: OpenOblivion desktop build with the hull receipt, original 20-step stair fixture, software GL, one async physics worker
finding:hull-needs-support-point-walkabi.oracle: same-binary fixtures: hull-only ratio 1.42; with the walkability patch view variation fell 31% (ascent), 34% (descent) and 43% (Vilverin) against the template box
finding:hull-needs-support-point-walkabi.unverified: The original controller's own stepping rules are unmeasured; the rule fits the observed support-under-apex contact but is a port choice; phone feel of the hull build is pending.

finding:kf-transform-clips-decoded.name: kf-transform-clips-decoded
finding:kf-transform-clips-decoded.summary: Oblivion 20.0.0.4 KF sequences (NiControllerSequence with string-palette bone names, compressed cubic-spline channels, NIF WXYZ rotation layout) decode to 73 transform tracks for the idle and forward-walk clips; an independent PyFFI parse and de Boor evaluator agreed within 7.3e-7 on 1,525 samples.
finding:kf-transform-clips-decoded.build: owner's third-person idle and forward-walking clips, NIF version 20.0.0.4
finding:kf-transform-clips-decoded.oracle: independent PyFFI parse plus a separately written float64 de Boor evaluator over 23 compressed tracks, tolerance 2e-5
finding:kf-transform-clips-decoded.unverified: Decoder measurements only: no original-executable playback or locomotion comparison; two float tracks and nine tail targets are skipped.

finding:mopp-bytecode-not-needed-for-sta.name: mopp-bytecode-not-needed-for-static-import
finding:mopp-bytecode-not-needed-for-sta.summary: A MOPP tree is an acceleration structure around its child shape: the child bhkNiTriStripsShape triangles can be loaded into a Bullet BVH without executing the MOPP bytes or shipping Havok's cooker.
finding:mopp-bytecode-not-needed-for-sta.build: OpenOblivion authored-strip loader on six stair meshes
finding:mopp-bytecode-not-needed-for-sta.oracle: the loader accepts MOPP-over-strips and builds a Bullet mesh whose AABB equals the visible mesh's on four of six stairs
finding:mopp-bytecode-not-needed-for-sta.unverified: That MOPP-culled Havok queries equal queries over the full triangle set (a MOPP built from a subset or different welding would differ) was not tested against Havok.

finding:oblivion-air-control-relaxation.name: oblivion-air-control-relaxation
finding:oblivion-air-control-relaxation.summary: While airborne the horizontal velocity relaxes toward the wanted ground velocity by v += f (wanted - v) per controller update, with f = fJumpMoveBase + fJumpMoveMult x Acrobatics / 100 (0 + 0.3 x 0.05 = 0.015 at Acrobatics 5; exe defaults 0 and 0.3). Momentum at takeoff is kept.
finding:oblivion-air-control-relaxation.build: owner's retail Steam Oblivion run unchanged under Proton, offline, 2026-10-06 (PE timestamp 0x462392c7); sampler read-only at 200 Hz
finding:oblivion-air-control-relaxation.oracle: Replay exact (0.000) on 28 airborne updates of a jump from a walk; +1.2 per update seen at run speed; at Acrobatics 100 the measured gain was 0.28 to 0.29 on stairs against 0.3 predicted.
finding:oblivion-air-control-relaxation.unverified: Gain at other Acrobatics values on flat floor; whether the wanted velocity is contact-projected; per-update (not per-second) means the effect scales with frame rate.

finding:oblivion-capture-keeps-velocity-.name: oblivion-capture-keeps-velocity-needs-descent
finding:oblivion-capture-keeps-velocity-.summary: The update that captures a fall (pre-move height inside the support range) switches the state to ground and keeps its velocity (no gravity added); the next update resets to -g*dt. Capture needs vz <= 0: a rising hull inside the range stays airborne (state 2).
finding:oblivion-capture-keeps-velocity-.oracle: captured updates move by exactly the previous vz*dt (e.g. 199.355 to 188.455 with vz -32.4466 at dt 0.048); takeoff updates of the recorded jumps
finding:oblivion-capture-keeps-velocity-.unverified: Penetration recovery is observed, not modelled.
finding:oblivion-capture-keeps-velocity-.note: A fast fall crosses the range in one step and penetrates the floor by about 1.5 units, then recovers 0.07 units per update (observed, not modelled).

finding:oblivion-character-proxy-classes.name: oblivion-character-proxy-classes
finding:oblivion-character-proxy-classes.summary: Oblivion.exe RTTI contains a Havok character-proxy controller family: bhkCharacterController, bhkCharacterProxy, bhkCharControllerShape, bhkCharacterPointCollector and states OnGround, InAir, Jumping, Swimming, Flying and Projectile.
finding:oblivion-character-proxy-classes.build: Steam retail Oblivion.exe (x86 PE32), PE timestamp 0x462392c7
finding:oblivion-character-proxy-classes.oracle: class names read from the RTTI dump; consistent with the runtime measurement that the player owns a character controller with a phantom and shape
finding:oblivion-character-proxy-classes.unverified: How each state is entered and what it does; whether the player uses every state; step and slope rules inside the proxy.

finding:oblivion-collision-mesh-not-rend.name: oblivion-collision-mesh-not-render-mesh
finding:oblivion-collision-mesh-not-rend.summary: Authored collision of the six stair meshes has about half the triangles of the visible mesh and a measurably different surface (arwhallstairs01: median height difference 2.32 units over 245 paired rays, maximum 372.7; arnhallstairs01 median 0.55): collision geometry is not render geometry.
finding:oblivion-collision-mesh-not-rend.build: owner's Oblivion Vilverin slice, six stair NIFs, desktop OpenMW 0.52 loader with the authored-strip switch on and off
finding:oblivion-collision-mesh-not-rend.oracle: 20 by 20 downward ray grid on each shape's own AABB, paired where the AABBs match
finding:oblivion-collision-mesh-not-rend.unverified: This is a shape trace, not a character-controller recording; its effect on stair feel is unmeasured.

finding:oblivion-controller-floats-above.name: oblivion-controller-floats-above-floor
finding:oblivion-controller-floats-above.summary: On flat floor the original controller's hull floats: its lowest point sits about 4 units above the floor triangles and its reference position about 2.25 units below them, so a port that rests the hull on the floor stands about 3.25 units higher.
finding:oblivion-controller-floats-above.build: same session as the hull measurement; Vilverin starting landing
finding:oblivion-controller-floats-above.oracle: contact manifold distance 3.3-3.4 units at three resting points (measured); the offsets assume the contact is the floor's outer surface including its own convex radius; port rested at Z 513.0 versus the original's 509.7 on the same landing
finding:oblivion-controller-floats-above.unverified: The surface assumption; the float is measured but not reproduced by the port.

finding:oblivion-controller-semi-implici.name: oblivion-controller-semi-implicit-per-frame
finding:oblivion-controller-semi-implici.summary: Each controller update subtracts g*dt from the vertical velocity and then moves by the new velocity, using that update's own frame time (no fixed sub-step), so the realised jump apex depends on frame rate: 69.0 units in the continuous limit, 66.8 at 60 Hz, 64.4 at 35 ms steps, 62.5 at 50 ms.
finding:oblivion-controller-semi-implici.build: owner's retail Steam Oblivion run unchanged under Proton, offline, 2026-10-06 (PE timestamp 0x462392c7); sampler read-only at 200 Hz
finding:oblivion-controller-semi-implici.oracle: Replay of the law over every logged airborne update with its own logged dt: residual 0.000 in position and velocity on 75, 28 and 18 updates, including a 166 ms frame.
finding:oblivion-controller-semi-implici.unverified: Hardware-GL frame rates (only about 28 Hz was recorded); behaviour at very large dt (clamping not seen).

finding:oblivion-controller-state-codes.name: oblivion-controller-state-codes
finding:oblivion-controller-state-codes.summary: The controller's current-state field reads 0 on ground, 1 jumping (one update, no motion) and 2 in air, in Havok's character-state order; a separate request field holds 11 when nothing is requested.
finding:oblivion-controller-state-codes.build: owner's retail Steam Oblivion run unchanged under Proton, offline, 2026-10-06 (PE timestamp 0x462392c7); sampler read-only at 200 Hz
finding:oblivion-controller-state-codes.oracle: Observed across standing, walking, jumping and landing at 200 Hz; the state-update functions were located through RTTI and read statically.

finding:oblivion-ground-speed-from-setti.name: oblivion-ground-speed-from-settings
finding:oblivion-ground-speed-from-setti.summary: The original computes player ground speed from game settings (walk min/max blended by the Speed attribute, an encumbrance term, no-weapon and sneak multipliers; run multiplies by a run multiplier plus an athletics term), not from animation state.
finding:oblivion-ground-speed-from-setti.build: Steam retail Oblivion.exe as read by the OpenOblivion project, with the owner's Oblivion.esm settings
finding:oblivion-ground-speed-from-setti.oracle: the character speed routine and the settings it registers read in the executable; a private sample of the original walking down stairs peaked at 117.3 units/s against the formula's 116.6 for a sheathed walk
finding:oblivion-ground-speed-from-setti.unverified: Run speed was never sampled in the original; carried weight, skill changes and swim speed are unmodelled; one walking sample, from the same project.

finding:oblivion-grounded-hover-resets-v.name: oblivion-grounded-hover-resets-velocity
finding:oblivion-grounded-hover-resets-v.summary: While supported on level ground the controller sets vz = -g*dt every update (no accumulation), so the hull sinks g*dt^2 per update (1.19 units at 48 ms, 0.56 at 33 ms, 0.14 at 16.7 ms) until it rests: a hover of up to 14 units that lasts about a second at 60 Hz.
finding:oblivion-grounded-hover-resets-v.oracle: exact replay of about 120 grounded updates (position and velocity) at two frame rates
finding:oblivion-grounded-hover-resets-v.unverified: The 60 Hz duration is extrapolated (nothing above 30 Hz was recorded); walkable slopes; whether the original floats downhill at 60 fps.

finding:oblivion-grounded-state-falls-un.name: oblivion-grounded-state-falls-under-gravity
finding:oblivion-grounded-state-falls-un.summary: On a stair flight the controller stays in the ground state while vz accumulates by g*dt each update (a free fall per tread: ratios -1.96 ... -10.5 over ten updates), and resets to -g*dt on the level landing; on level ground it resets every update (finding:oblivion-grounded-hover-resets-velocity). The discriminator is inferred to be the contact's classification (supported or sliding).
finding:oblivion-grounded-state-falls-un.build: owner's retail Steam Oblivion run unchanged under Proton, offline, 2026-10-06 (PE timestamp 0x462392c7); sampler read-only at 200 Hz
finding:oblivion-grounded-state-falls-un.oracle: Per-update traces of a walk down a stair flight and of three standing jumps; the phantom centre stays 71 units above the reference position, so it is the body; the ground and air states are told apart by a support flag the executable sets after each integration.
finding:oblivion-grounded-state-falls-un.unverified: The classification rule (slope limit, which contact normal is used: the downward hull sweep's normal did not reproduce it, EXP-OO-019); behaviour at 60 fps; other surfaces.
finding:oblivion-grounded-state-falls-un.note: Stair descent at 36 ms: drops of 1.3 to 6 units per update, horizontal speed 12.8 against 16.76 Havok units/s on those contacts. Revised 2026-10-08: the 2026-10-06 reading (gravity accumulates on the ground, resets on contact) holds only for steep contacts.

finding:oblivion-havok-wrapper-classes.name: oblivion-havok-wrapper-classes
finding:oblivion-havok-wrapper-classes.summary: Oblivion.exe RTTI names a full Havok wrapper layer: collision objects (static, phantom, blend), shapes (MOPP tree, tri-strips, packed tri-strips, convex vertices, box, capsule, list, sphere, plane, cylinder, height field), phantoms, listeners and a constraint family (ball-and-socket, hinge, limited hinge, prismatic, ragdoll, stiff spring, malleable, fixed, generic, wheel).
finding:oblivion-havok-wrapper-classes.build: Steam retail Oblivion.exe (x86 PE32), PE timestamp 0x462392c7
finding:oblivion-havok-wrapper-classes.oracle: class names read from the RTTI dump with rtti_scan.py (85 bhk*, 51 hk*, 5 Havok* classes); names only, no behaviour read
finding:oblivion-havok-wrapper-classes.unverified: Which classes the shipped data actually uses; a class existing in the exe does not mean any NIF instantiates it.

finding:oblivion-jump-height-formula.name: oblivion-jump-height-formula
finding:oblivion-jump-height-formula.summary: Jump height is fJumpHeightMin + (fJumpHeightMax - fJumpHeightMin) x Acrobatics / 100; the launch speed is sqrt(2 g h) and the horizontal velocity is kept. Controller height fields read 69, 114 and 164 units at Acrobatics 5, 50 and 100 (min 64 exe default, max 164 master override).
finding:oblivion-jump-height-formula.build: owner's retail Steam Oblivion run unchanged under Proton, offline, 2026-10-06 (PE timestamp 0x462392c7); sampler read-only at 200 Hz
finding:oblivion-jump-height-formula.oracle: Formula read statically from the jump routine; value read from the live controller at three Acrobatics values; first airborne velocity equals sqrt(2 g h) - g dt to four decimals each time (replay residual about 4e-6).
finding:oblivion-jump-height-formula.unverified: Encumbrance, fatigue cost and perks (only the base formula was checked); creatures and NPCs.

finding:oblivion-player-hull-convex-not-.name: oblivion-player-hull-convex-not-capsule
finding:oblivion-player-hull-convex-not-.summary: The live player controller shape is an 18-vertex convex hull, not a capsule: an eight-sided prism (ring radius 20.25 units) with a pointed cone at each end, 128 units tall, convex radius 0.70, identical while standing, walking, jumping and sneaking, and rotating with heading.
finding:oblivion-player-hull-convex-not-.build: owner's retail Steam Oblivion run unchanged under Proton, offline, 2026-10-03; exe build not recorded in the source document
finding:oblivion-player-hull-convex-not-.oracle: read-only 20 Hz sampler of the running process memory (player reference, controller, phantom, shape) across standing, walking stairs, jumping, sneaking, turning and three resting points; diagonal vertices agree with the executable's own cos 45 rounding
finding:oblivion-player-hull-convex-not-.unverified: Step height, slope limit, gait, acceleration, jump impulse, swimming and how race height scale changes the hull; one measurement session, one install, no second independent measurement.

finding:oblivion-rtti-full-msvc.name: oblivion-rtti-full-msvc
finding:oblivion-rtti-full-msvc.summary: The Steam retail Oblivion.exe has complete MSVC RTTI: 1,715 vtables for 1,482 classes are recoverable, including the whole Ni* scene graph, the TES* forms and the Havok bhk*/hk* wrapper classes.
finding:oblivion-rtti-full-msvc.build: Steam retail Oblivion.exe (x86 PE32), PE timestamp 0x462392c7 (2007-04-16)
finding:oblivion-rtti-full-msvc.oracle: rtti_scan.py over the exe's data sections; RTTI base lists agree with known class hierarchies; runs in 0.15 s
finding:oblivion-rtti-full-msvc.unverified: Struct layouts and behaviour of the classes; other Oblivion builds (GOG, patched executables) were not scanned.

finding:oblivion-run-speed-355-6.name: oblivion-run-speed-355-6
finding:oblivion-run-speed-355-6.summary: The player's run speed is 355.6 units/s with Speed 40, Athletics 5 and the weapon sheathed: the live controller's first velocity after Shift+W equals the formula's run branch, walk x (fMoveRunMult + fMoveRunAthleticsMult x Athletics / 100).
finding:oblivion-run-speed-355-6.build: owner's retail Steam Oblivion run unchanged under Proton, offline, 2026-10-06 (PE timestamp 0x462392c7); sampler read-only at 200 Hz
finding:oblivion-run-speed-355-6.oracle: Controller velocity read at 200 Hz during Shift+W on the running original; matches the statically decoded formula to 0.1.
finding:oblivion-run-speed-355-6.unverified: Weapon drawn, sneak run, encumbrance and other stats; slope contacts reduce the realised horizontal speed.

finding:oblivion-stair-collision-strips-.name: oblivion-stair-collision-strips-unscaled
finding:oblivion-stair-collision-strips-.summary: On the six stair meshes of the Vilverin slice the collision vertices live in the bhkNiTriStripsShape's NiTriStripsData in visible-mesh units: bounds match the visible mesh on four of six, MOPP scale is 1 and strip scale is (1,1,1,0), so the packed-vertex factor of 7 must not be applied.
finding:oblivion-stair-collision-strips-.build: owner's Oblivion Vilverin visual slice: six stair NIFs, version 20.0.0.4, user version 11/10, decoded with the OpenMW 0.52 NIF reader
finding:oblivion-stair-collision-strips-.oracle: collision bounds compared with visible-mesh bounds per axis on all six meshes; the x7 variant came out about seven times too large
finding:oblivion-stair-collision-strips-.unverified: Packed strip shapes (zero blocks in this slice) do use the factor in niftools; U-turn and pit meshes differ by a few percent for other reasons; Fallout 3 and Skyrim not checked.

finding:oblivion-stairs-static-layer.name: oblivion-stairs-static-layer
finding:oblivion-stairs-static-layer.summary: All six Vilverin stair meshes are fixed OL_STATIC (layer 1) stone bodies with mass 0, friction 0.3 and restitution 0.3; none uses the OL_STAIRS layer (19) or the stone-stairs material, so walkability on them cannot depend on a special stair layer.
finding:oblivion-stairs-static-layer.build: owner's Oblivion Vilverin visual slice, six stair NIFs (arnhallstairs01, arnhallstairsentrance01, arnhalluturnstairs02, arwhallstairs01, arwhallstairsbridge01, arpitstairs02)
finding:oblivion-stairs-static-layer.oracle: block fields decoded for each stair body with the 20.0.0.4 layout; layer, material, motion and quality read directly
finding:oblivion-stairs-static-layer.unverified: Stairs in other tilesets and in later games may use OL_STAIRS; the player controller's own use of layer or material is not measured.

finding:oblivion-support-range-2-havok.name: oblivion-support-range-2-havok
finding:oblivion-support-range-2-havok.summary: The player controller counts as supported while the ground is less than 2.0 Havok units (13.998 game units) below its resting height: placed 13.8 units above rest it stays grounded, at 14.0, 14.2, 14.5 and 15.1 it leaves the ground at the first update (bracket 1.9717 to 2.0003 Havok); beyond the range it falls with ordinary gravity and is recaptured inside it.
finding:oblivion-support-range-2-havok.build: owner's retail Steam Oblivion run unchanged under Proton, offline, 2026-10-08 (PE timestamp 0x462392c7); sampler read-only at 200 Hz; software GL at about 21 and 30 updates/s
finding:oblivion-support-range-2-havok.oracle: player.setpos z placement at 5 to 125 units above a flat floor, per-update states and heights replayed with the logged step times (residual 0.05 units, rounding of the recording)
finding:oblivion-support-range-2-havok.unverified: Range on slopes and stair nosings; whether it scales with anything but the hull; behaviour at 60 fps.

finding:oblivion-world-gravity-73-575.name: oblivion-world-gravity-73-575
finding:oblivion-world-gravity-73-575.summary: The original's Havok world gravity is (0, 0, -73.575) Havok units/s^2 (9.81 x 7.5), about 514.95 game units/s^2 (a Havok unit is 1/0.1428767293691635 game units, the executable's own constant). A controller gravity scale of 1.0 multiplies it.
finding:oblivion-world-gravity-73-575.build: owner's retail Steam Oblivion run unchanged under Proton, offline, 2026-10-06 (PE timestamp 0x462392c7); sampler read-only at 200 Hz
finding:oblivion-world-gravity-73-575.oracle: Read from the live Havok world object while the game ran; the same value reproduces every logged vertical-velocity step (g x dt) to four decimals.
finding:oblivion-world-gravity-73-575.unverified: Other builds; whether other objects (projectiles, ragdolls, horses) use the same value.

finding:openmw-actor-constants-are-morro.name: openmw-actor-constants-are-morrowind
finding:openmw-actor-constants-are-morro.summary: OpenMW 0.52's actor is a Bullet shape from the rendered bounds with step-up 34, step-down 62 and maximum slope 46 degrees; these are Morrowind-era constants, not Oblivion records, and mwphysics contains no btKinematicCharacterController (it has its own movement solver and stepper).
finding:openmw-actor-constants-are-morro.oracle: constants read in components/misc/constants.hpp and apps/openmw/mwphysics/constants.hpp; grep of apps/openmw/mwphysics finds no btKinematicCharacterController and lists movementsolver and stepper sources
finding:openmw-actor-constants-are-morro.unverified: The actor-shape-from-bounds detail comes from the project doc, not re-read; later revisions untested.

finding:openmw-pin-ignores-bhk-collision.name: openmw-pin-ignores-bhk-collision
finding:openmw-pin-ignores-bhk-collision.summary: At the pinned OpenMW 0.52 revision and the Android 0.51 base, TES4 NIF collision is generated from the visible geometry when BSXFlags bit 2 is set; the reader parses bhkCollisionObject, bhkRigidBody, bhkMoppBvTreeShape and bhkNiTriStripsShape but the Bullet loader consumes none of them.
finding:openmw-pin-ignores-bhk-collision.build: OpenMW 0.52 at 46bd4599203ee52ffc0f3e8edb3fc159a0303a49 (desktop pin) and the Android 0.51 base f4bec41444214a7903bebd178389ca22ca13f646
finding:openmw-pin-ignores-bhk-collision.oracle: components/nifbullet/bulletnifloader.cpp read at both pinned revisions by the OpenOblivion project (its docs cite file and line)
finding:openmw-pin-ignores-bhk-collision.unverified: Later OpenMW revisions may differ; the loader itself was not re-read for this record.

finding:silent-model-failure-error-marke.name: silent-model-failure-error-marker
finding:silent-model-failure-error-marke.summary: When a model fails to load the donor engine substitutes an embedded error-marker mesh: a malformed player collision model became a 123-unit-wide body that could not pass a 111-unit doorway, which looked like a collision bug.
finding:silent-model-failure-error-marke.build: OpenOblivion 0.18 on the OpenMW pins; OSG 3.6.5 ASCII reader
finding:silent-model-failure-error-marke.oracle: the old file reproduces the parser errors and the blockage; the corrected file loads and the player crosses after the gate opens (native before/after probes; ARM64 OSG harness on an emulator)

finding:skeleton-names-differ-from-donor.name: skeleton-names-differ-from-donor-expectation
finding:skeleton-names-differ-from-donor.summary: Oblivion's male skeleton NIF has 370 blocks and 142 named nodes (Bip01 Pelvis, Bip01 Spine, Bip01 Spine1...) but no Groin, Chest, Neck, Head or Right Hand nodes, so donor code that attaches parts by Morrowind bone names fails with a Groin error.
finding:skeleton-names-differ-from-donor.oracle: node names listed from the skeleton NIF with the pinned reader; the phone log shows the Groin lookup error
finding:skeleton-names-differ-from-donor.unverified: The beast skeleton (426 blocks, 160 names) was read the same way; the name mapping between the two schemes is not recorded here.

finding:touch-overlay-covered-use-button.name: touch-overlay-covered-use-button
finding:touch-overlay-covered-use-button.summary: At the Vilverin hall gate a thirteen-button touch overlay covered the right half of the screen including USE and the phone log had no activation line; the overlay was reduced to a move stick plus four buttons.
finding:touch-overlay-covered-use-button.build: OpenOblivion phone build 0.10-touch-name, report from the owner's phone
finding:touch-overlay-covered-use-button.oracle: the absent activation log line while the center ray read the gate; the layout of the old overlay
finding:touch-overlay-covered-use-button.unverified: Phone retest of the reduced overlay is pending; the engine's same-cell door handler also hides the door for five seconds instead of animating it.

game:black-and-white.name: Black & White

game:morrowind.name: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind

game:oblivion.name: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
game:oblivion.summary: Bethesda's 2006 RPG on Gamebryo with Havok; the Windows x86 Steam build is the reference build for the OpenOblivion port and for most measurements in this compendium.

game:ogre-battle-64.summary: N64 game statically recompiled to a native PC executable with N64Recomp.

game:sonic-unleashed.name: Sonic Unleashed
game:sonic-unleashed.summary: Xbox 360 game statically recompiled to Windows and Linux by UnleashedRecomp.

game:zelda-majoras-mask.name: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask
game:zelda-majoras-mask.summary: N64 game with a static-recompilation PC port built on N64Recomp.

platform:android-arm64.name: Android ARM64
platform:android-arm64.summary: Phones; the target platform of OpenOblivion and most mobile ports.

platform:android-x86_64-emulator.name: Android x86_64 emulator
platform:android-x86_64-emulator.summary: Stock KVM emulator images; run arm64 apps through a translation layer unless the app ships x86_64 libraries.

platform:n64.name: Nintendo 64
platform:n64.summary: MIPS (VR4300) console; source platform of N64Recomp-based ports.

platform:windows-x64.name: Windows x64
platform:windows-x64.summary: 64-bit Windows PE executables (Unity players, Unreal games, modern titles).

platform:windows-x86.name: Windows x86 (32-bit PC)
platform:windows-x86.summary: 32-bit Windows PE executables, the original platform of Oblivion and Black & White.

platform:xbox360.name: Xbox 360
platform:xbox360.summary: PowerPC console; source platform of XenonRecomp-based ports and of the New Vegas MemDebug decomp.

problem:android-emulator-gles-crash.name: arm64 app crashes in the x86_64 emulator at scene start
problem:android-emulator-gles-crash.summary: SIGSEGV with fault address 0 in the ARM translation layer's GLES proxy when an arm64-only app first renders.

problem:android-startup-deadlock.name: Android start-up hang with a splash window
problem:android-startup-deadlock.summary: Process alive at 0% CPU, only a splash window, log stops after onCreate.

problem:compiler-tiebreak-mismatch.name: Matching residual caused by a compiler tie-break
problem:compiler-tiebreak-mismatch.summary: A function differs only in operand or register order that depends on earlier compiler state, not on what the source means.

problem:jump-height-mismatch.name: Jump height does not match the formula
problem:jump-height-mismatch.summary: A measured jump apex differs from the documented formula; in a controller that integrates with the frame time the apex depends on frame rate, and a ceiling or a single sample can mislead.

problem:silent-asset-load-failure.name: Failed model load substituted by an error marker
problem:silent-asset-load-failure.summary: A model that fails to load is replaced by an embedded marker mesh, so a body or prop silently has the wrong size.

problem:skeleton-bone-name-mismatch.name: Skeleton loads but parts or animations bind wrongly
problem:skeleton-bone-name-mismatch.summary: The donor looks bones up by another game's names, or parts copy a private skeleton, so animation does not reach the mesh.

problem:stair-camera-jolt.name: Per-tread camera jolt on stairs
problem:stair-camera-jolt.summary: Each stair tread produces a vertical view jolt even though ascent and descent work.

problem:tes4-collision-fidelity.name: TES4 collision fidelity
problem:tes4-collision-fidelity.summary: The donor engine builds collision from visible geometry while the original used authored Havok shapes; surfaces differ measurably.

problem:tes4-movement-parity.name: TES4 movement parity
problem:tes4-movement-parity.summary: Matching the original player's speed, body, stepping and jump on a donor engine.

problem:touch-overlay-blocks-actions.name: Touch overlay reaches the UI but gameplay actions do nothing
problem:touch-overlay-blocks-actions.summary: A touch overlay can cover or swallow the action button, or the engine's default handler can fire without visible effect.

project:bw1-decomp.name: Black & White decompilation
project:bw1-decomp.summary: MSVC 6 matching decomp (dtk, objdiff); its AGENTS.md records inline-budget analysis and which dead ends to stop chasing.

project:fallout1-ce.name: Fallout CE (Fallout 1)
project:fallout1-ce.summary: Playable drop-in reimplementation of Fallout 1 with bug fixes and quality-of-life options, reading the user's data files.

project:fnv-decomp.name: Fallout: New Vegas MemDebug decomp
project:fnv-decomp.summary: Xbox 360 MemDebug reconstruction of Gamebryo 2.2 and TES* headers; useful for naming orientation only. AI policy: human-only.

project:fromsoftware-rs.name: fromsoftware-rs
project:fromsoftware-rs.summary: Rust pattern library for runtime modding of x64 MSVC games with RTTI-derived class bindings and an AOB-to-RVA mapper.

project:halo-ce-decomp.name: Halo CE decompilation
project:halo-ce-decomp.summary: Xbox cachebeta.exe (build 2342) decomp: tag system, module layout, objdiff-based progress.

project:n64recomp.name: N64Recomp
project:n64recomp.summary: Static recompiler from N64 machine code to C (MIT); inputs are the ROM, an ELF with symbols and relocations, and a TOML config; the runtime lives in N64ModernRuntime.

project:ogre-battle-64-recomp.name: Ogre Battle 64 recomp
project:ogre-battle-64-recomp.summary: Ogre Battle 64 recompiled with the N64Recomp toolchain to a native PC executable.

project:openoblivion.name: OpenOblivion
project:openoblivion.summary: 1:1 port of Oblivion for Android on a patched OpenMW; owner's project and the first consumer of this compendium; the source of most movement and collision records here.

project:unleashedrecomp.name: UnleashedRecomp
project:unleashedrecomp.summary: Static recompilation of Sonic Unleashed (Xbox 360) with a Windows/Linux runtime layer and an installer that dumps the user's own content.

project:xenonrecomp.name: XenonRecomp
project:xenonrecomp.summary: PPC-to-C++ static recompiler for Xbox 360 titles (with XenosRecomp for shaders) used by UnleashedRecomp and MarathonRecomp.

project:zelda64recomp.name: Zelda 64: Recompiled
project:zelda64recomp.summary: Native PC port of Majora's Mask built on N64Recomp. AI policy: human-only, so never contribute with AI help.

struct:bhkBlendCollisionObject.name: bhkBlendCollisionObject
struct:bhkBlendCollisionObject.summary: Collision object blended with animation, the ragdoll path (with bhkBlendController).

struct:bhkBoxShape.name: bhkBoxShape
struct:bhkBoxShape.summary: Box primitive; half-extents multiplied by 7 reproduced the visible door slabs.

struct:bhkCapsuleShape.name: bhkCapsuleShape
struct:bhkCapsuleShape.summary: Capsule primitive, used in ragdoll limbs (the player skeleton's capsules are layer-8 limbs, not the controller).

struct:bhkCharacterController.name: bhkCharacterController
struct:bhkCharacterController.summary: Oblivion's Havok character-controller family: controller, proxy, controller shape and OnGround/InAir/Jumping/Swimming/Flying/Projectile states.

struct:bhkCollisionObject.name: bhkCollisionObject
struct:bhkCollisionObject.summary: NIF block that attaches a rigid body (and so a Havok shape) to a scene node; phantom and blend variants have their own classes.

struct:bhkConvexVerticesShape.name: bhkConvexVerticesShape
struct:bhkConvexVerticesShape.summary: Convex hull collision shape, common for clutter and props.

struct:bhkMoppBvTreeShape.name: bhkMoppBvTreeShape
struct:bhkMoppBvTreeShape.summary: Havok bounding-volume tree code wrapped around a child shape; an acceleration structure whose bytes need not be executed to import the child triangles.

struct:bhkNiTriStripsShape.name: bhkNiTriStripsShape
struct:bhkNiTriStripsShape.summary: Triangle-strip collision shape that references NiTriStripsData; in the measured stair meshes its vertices are already in visible-mesh units.

struct:bhkPackedNiTriStripsShape.name: bhkPackedNiTriStripsShape
aliases: bhk packed ni tri strips shape
struct:bhkPackedNiTriStripsShape.summary: Packed triangle collision shape; niftools documents a factor-of-7 vertex scale for it. Zero blocks occurred in the measured Oblivion slice.

struct:bhkRigidBody.name: bhkRigidBody
struct:bhkRigidBody.summary: Havok body: layer and filter, motion type (fixed, keyframed, dynamic), quality, mass, friction, restitution, and its shape.

struct:bhkSPCollisionObject.name: bhkSPCollisionObject
struct:bhkSPCollisionObject.summary: Collision object for a phantom (a volume that reports overlaps without pushing); used for trigger volumes.

subsystem:android-port.name: Android port runtime
subsystem:android-port.summary: Building, installing, launching and testing a native engine on Android phones and emulators.

subsystem:animation.name: Animation and skeletons
subsystem:animation.summary: Skeleton node trees, keyframe sequences (KF), skinning and part attachment.

subsystem:archive-parsing.name: Archive parsing
subsystem:archive-parsing.summary: Reading container formats (BSA, BA2, VPK, pak): headers, directory tables, name tables, offsets, last-entry handling.

subsystem:binary-recon.name: Executable recon
subsystem:binary-recon.summary: Understanding a binary without source: triage, RTTI classes, string-to-function pivots, tables, signatures.

subsystem:camera.name: Camera / view
subsystem:camera.summary: Camera placement and filtering: eye height, tracking the player root, smoothing, collision of the camera itself.

subsystem:collision.name: Collision geometry
subsystem:collision.summary: Static and dynamic collision shapes, their layers/filters/materials, and how authored collision relates to visible geometry.

subsystem:input-ui.name: Input and UI routing
subsystem:input-ui.summary: Getting a device event to the right layer: overlay hit-testing, UI versus gameplay, action bindings, menus that must always be closable.

subsystem:matching-decomp.name: Function matching workflow
subsystem:matching-decomp.summary: Making recompiled source equal the original object code byte for byte, function by function.

subsystem:player-controller.name: Player / character controller
subsystem:player-controller.summary: Moving the player body through the world: body shape, ground test, step-up and step-down, slopes, jumping, gait and speed.

subsystem:ragdoll-constraints.name: Ragdoll and constraints
subsystem:ragdoll-constraints.summary: Constrained rigid-body chains (ragdolls, hinges, springs) blended with animation.

subsystem:rendering-gl.name: Rendering and GL
subsystem:rendering-gl.summary: Renderer, GL/GLES driver and translation layers, shaders and textures.

subsystem:scripting.name: Script compiler and runtime
subsystem:scripting.summary: Compiling or interpreting a game's script language (TES4 script source and bytecode, command tables).

subsystem:triggers-phantoms.name: Triggers and phantoms
subsystem:triggers-phantoms.summary: Volumes that report overlap without blocking: trigger boxes, scripted regions, detection.

tech:bullet.name: Bullet Physics
tech:bullet.summary: Open-source physics library used by OpenMW and the usual open backend for translating authored Havok collision.

tech:gl4es.name: GL4ES
tech:gl4es.summary: OpenGL-on-GLES translation layer used by OpenMW-Android style ports; its load-time EGL call is part of a known start-up deadlock.

tech:havok.name: Havok Physics
tech:havok.summary: Commercial physics middleware used by Gamebryo-era Bethesda games; Oblivion wraps it in bhk* classes and stores collision in NIF blocks.

tech:opengl-es.name: OpenGL ES
tech:opengl-es.summary: Mobile graphics API; an arm64 app reaching it through the emulator's ARM translation layer is where the known emulator crash occurs.

tech:speedtree.name: SpeedTree
tech:speedtree.summary: Tree middleware; Oblivion ships trees as .spt data with SpeedTree* shader classes in the exe.

technique:android-emulator-gate.name: Android emulator gate
technique:android-emulator-gate.summary: Scripted adb checks (launch, engine thread, stable frames, menu, BACK) on an x86_64 emulator with a native x86_64 build of the port.

technique:aob-signatures.name: AOB signatures
technique:aob-signatures.summary: Version-robust byte patterns with wildcards for moving operands; re-verify on every build.

technique:authored-collision-translation.name: Authored collision translation
technique:authored-collision-translation.summary: Translate a game's authored collision blocks into an open physics backend's shapes (static triangle meshes first), filtering by layer; skip what is acceleration data.

technique:hash-locked-receipts.name: Hash-locked patch receipts
technique:hash-locked-receipts.summary: Carry engine changes as a script plus lock file plus per-platform patches plus tests, so any native change can be regenerated and audited.

technique:msvc-rtti-recovery.name: MSVC RTTI recovery
technique:msvc-rtti-recovery.summary: Recover C++ class names, vtables and inheritance from MSVC run-time type information with rtti_scan.py, no disassembler needed.

technique:paired-same-binary-probe.name: Paired same-binary probe
technique:paired-same-binary-probe.summary: Compare raw versus changed behaviour with the same build, the same scripted driver and the same start placement, using a named metric; compare rows, not single digits.

technique:replay-oracle.name: Per-update replay oracle
technique:replay-oracle.summary: Sample a running original read-only at several times its update rate, collapse the samples into the game's own updates and replay a candidate law over each one with the logged step time; a right law leaves zero residual.

technique:round-trip-oracle.name: Round-trip oracle
technique:round-trip-oracle.summary: Decode, re-encode and compare with the original bytes (or a stated error bound) to prove a parser or format reading.

technique:runtime-memory-sampler.name: Runtime memory sampler
technique:runtime-memory-sampler.summary: Read-only sampling of an owned single-player game's process memory at a fixed rate to measure live structures (controller shape, positions). Offline only; no anti-cheat involved; nothing is written to the process.

technique:static-initializer-scan.name: Static-initializer scan
technique:static-initializer-scan.summary: Recover compiled-in setting defaults by scanning the instruction patterns of static initializers that register each setting.

technique:string-xref-pivot.name: String to function pivot
technique:string-xref-pivot.summary: Find the code (or table) that references a string to locate a feature; strings referenced only from data point to tables.
